source.title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let S+ and S− denote the forward and backward shift operators acting on z(N0). In the five-case classification discussed in Section 2.1, determine whether case 3 can actually occur; equivalently, determine whether the range M(I − 2S−|z) can be a closed subspace of finite positive codimension 1, 2, 3, ....

evidence.quote: The preceding considerations lead to a rough classification of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals. The cases 1, 2, and 5 actually occur, while cases 3 and 4 are questionable; see Problems 1 and 2.
3. M(I − 2S−|z) is closed and cod ( M(I − 2S−|z) ) = 1, 2,....
Problem 1. Find out whether case 3 is impossible.

accepted.question_text: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let S− be the backward shift on z(N0). Determine whether case 4 from Section 2.1 can occur; that is, determine whether the range M(I − 2S−|z) can be closed and have infinite codimension.

evidence.quote: 4. M(I − 2S−|z) is closed and cod ( M(I − 2S−|z) ) = ∞.

The preceding considerations lead to a rough classification of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals. The cases 1, 2, and 5 actually occur, while cases 3 and 4 are questionable; see Problems 1 and 2.
Problem 2. Find out whether case 4 is impossible.

accepted.question_text: For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let S− be the backward shift operator on z(N0) and let r(S−|z) be its spectral radius. Determine whether the full spectrum of S− is exactly the closed disk {λ ∈ C : |λ| ≤ r(S−|z)}.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Find out whether σ(S−|z) = { λ ∈ C : |λ| ≤ r(S−|z) }.

accepted.question_text: For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let S+ and S− be the forward and backward shifts on z(N0). If σΦ denotes the Φ-spectrum, determine whether the Φ-spectrum of each shift is exactly the annulus σΦ(S±|z) = { λ ∈ C : r(S∓|z)^−1 ≤ |λ| ≤ r(S±|z) }.

evidence.quote: The Φ-spectrum of an operator S ∈ L(X) is defined by σΦ(S|X) := { λ ∈ C : λI − S ∉ Φ(X) }.
Problem 4. Find out whether σΦ(S±|z) = { λ ∈ C : r(S∓|z)−1 ≤ |λ| ≤ r(S±|z) }.

accepted.question_text: Let z(N0) be a shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let LAPP_z be the operator ideal consisting of operators S whose dyadic approximation-number sequence (a_{2^k}(S)) belongs to z(N0). Determine whether every trace on LAPP_z is one of the traces constructed in Theorem 1.19 from a 1/2 S+-invariant linear form on z(N0), so that LAPP_z supports no additional traces beyond that family.

evidence.quote: Given any shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), we let LAPP_z := { S ∈ L : (a_{2^k}(S)) ∈ z(N0) }.
Theorem 1.19. For every 1/2 S+-invariant linear form ϕ on z(N0), ... This definition yields a trace ϕz on LAPP_z.
Problem 5. Show that on LAPP_z there exist no other traces than those provided by Theorem 1.19.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r, and let AAPP_{r,∞} denote the ideal of operators S in A whose dyadic A-approximation numbers satisfy a_{2^k}(S|A) = O(2^{-k/r}). Determine whether every trace on AAPP_{r,∞} is one of the traces produced by Theorem 1.21, so that no additional traces exist on AAPP_{r,∞}.

evidence.quote: Given any shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), we let AAPP_z := { S ∈ A : (a_{2^k}(S|A)) ∈ z(N0) }.
Letting 0 < r < ∞, we consider the special Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal d_{r,∞}(N0) := { a = (αh) : |αh| = O(1/2^{h/r}) } ... The associated operator ideal is denoted by AAPP_{r,∞}.
Theorem 1.21. Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r. Then ... This definition yields a trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |A) on AAPP_{r,∞}.
Problem 6. Show that on AAPP_{r,∞} there exist no other traces than those provided by Theorem 1.21.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every norm-closed operator ideal is traceless, meaning that it admits no nonzero trace.

evidence.quote: An operator ideal A is called traceless if there does not exist any trace τ ≠ o. Otherwise, we say that A supports non-vanishing traces.
Problem 7. Show that all norm–closed operator ideals are traceless.

accepted.question_text: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. Determine whether every trace on LAPP_z is spectral, in the sense that for each operator S the trace is determined by the eigenvalue sequence of S through the dyadic block sums described in Section 2.4.

evidence.quote: A trace τ is called spectral if τ(S) can be reconstructed from the eigenvalue sequence (λ_n(S)) for all S ∈ A(X). More precisely, we require that τ(S) = ϕ( 1/2^k Σ_{n∈D_k} λ_n(S) ), where ϕ(a) := τ(D_a) for D_a ∈ A(ℓ2).
Problem 8. Show that all traces on LAPP_z are spectral whenever z(N0) is quasi-Banach.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r, and let ϕ_{r,∞}(·|A) be the trace on AAPP_{r,∞} constructed in Theorem 1.21. Determine whether this trace is spectral, i.e. whether it is completely determined by the eigenvalue sequence of each operator in the sense of Section 2.4.

evidence.quote: Theorem 1.21. Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r. Then ... This definition yields a trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |A) on AAPP_{r,∞}.
Problem 9. Find out whether the trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |A) on AAPP_{r,∞} presented in Theorem 1.21 is spectral.

accepted.question_text: For 1 ≤ r ≤ 2, let P_{r,2} be the ideal of (r,2)-summing operators, and let (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} be the operator ideal from Theorem 2.4. Determine whether every trace on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} is one of the traces constructed in Theorem 2.4, so that no additional traces exist on this ideal.

evidence.quote: Concerning the basics about P_{r,2}, the ideal of (r, 2)-summing operators ...
Theorem 2.4. ... This definition yields a trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |P_{r,2}) on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞}.
Problem 10. Show that on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} there exist no other traces than those provided by Theorem 2.4.

accepted.question_text: For 1 ≤ r ≤ 2, let ϕ_{r,∞}(·|P_{r,2}) denote the trace on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} from Theorem 2.4. Determine whether this trace is spectral.

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.4. ... This definition yields a trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |P_{r,2}) on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞}.
Problem 11. Find out whether the trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |P_{r,2}) on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} is spectral.

accepted.question_text: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, let LWEYL_{r,∞} be the quasi-Banach operator ideal defined by the dyadic Weyl-number condition x_{2^k}(S) = O(2^{-k/r}). Determine whether the interpolated ideals (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} strictly increase as r varies over [2,∞), or whether they become constant on that range; in particular, decide whether (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞} might already equal LWEYL_{1,∞}.

evidence.quote: Letting 0 < r ≤ ∞, we define the quasi-Banach operator ideal LWEYL_{r,∞} := { S ∈ L : x_{2^k}(S) = O(1/2^{k/r}) }.
Problem 12. Find out whether (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} strictly increases with the exponent r ∈ [2,∞) or is constant. Even (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞} = LWEYL_{1,∞} should be taken into account.

accepted.question_text: For the (r,2)-summing ideal P_{r,2} and the Weyl-number ideal LWEYL_{r,∞}, determine whether the two derived operator ideals (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} and (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} actually coincide.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Show that (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} and (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} coincide.

accepted.question_text: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, let (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} be the operator ideal carrying the traces from Theorem 2.8. Determine whether every trace on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} is one of the traces given by Theorem 2.8.

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.8. ... This rule yields a trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |LWEYL_{r,∞}) on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞}.
Problem 14. Show that on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} there exist no other traces than those provided by Theorem 2.8.

accepted.question_text: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, determine whether the trace ϕ_{r,∞}(·|LWEYL_{r,∞}) on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} constructed in Theorem 2.8 is spectral.

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.8. ... This rule yields a trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |LWEYL_{r,∞}) on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞}.
Problem 15. Find out whether the trace ϕ_{r,∞}(· |LWEYL_{r,∞}) on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} is spectral.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the Weyl-number ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing traces; the author explicitly conjectures that it should even support non-vanishing singular spectral traces.

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Show that LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing traces.
In my opinion, LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing singular spectral traces with a probability of 99 %.

accepted.question_text: Let LENT_z be the operator ideal defined by the dyadic entropy-number condition (e_{2^k}(S)) ∈ z(N0). Determine whether LAPP_z is always contained in LENT_z for every shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0).

evidence.quote: Though entropy numbers do not possess all properties of s-numbers, LENT_z := { S ∈ L : (e_{2^k}(S)) ∈ z(N0) } is still an operator ideal for every shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0).
Problem 17. Show that LAPP_z ⊆ LENT_z for all shift-monotone sequence ideals.

accepted.question_text: Find shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0) for which the entropy-number ideal LENT_z carries non-vanishing singular traces.

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Find shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0) such that LENT_z carries non-vanishing singular traces.

accepted.question_text: Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y, and let 0 < r < s < ∞ be large. Construct concrete operators S belonging to LAPP_{s,∞}(X,Y) but not to LAPP_{r,∞}(X,Y).

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Assuming that both indices 0 < r < s < ∞ are large, we want to find ‘concrete’ operators S ∈ LAPP_{s,∞}(X, Y ) \ LAPP_{r,∞}(X, Y ).

accepted.question_text: Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y. Find large families Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that (i) Z contains every Lorentz-type ideal d_{r,w}(N0), and (ii) the map z(N0) ↦ LAPP_z(X,Y) is injective on Z.

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Fix any pair of infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y. Find large sets Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals that have the following properties: (1) Z contains all d_{r,w}(N0). (2) The restriction of the map z(N0) → LAPP_z(X, Y ) to Z is one-to-one.

accepted.question_text: Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X that have few approximable operators, in the sense that app(X) is strictly smaller than the cone c0*(N) of nonincreasing null sequences; ideally, make app(X) as small as possible.

evidence.quote: For every infinite-dimensional Banach space X, we define the set app(X) := { (σ_n) ∈ c*_0(N) : σ_n ≼ a_n(S) for some S ∈ C_0(X) }. A Banach space X is said to have few approximable operators whenever app(X) is strictly smaller than c*_0(N).
Problem 21. Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces that have few approximable operators. Main goal: Make app(X) as small as possible.

accepted.question_text: Find Banach spaces that contain an unconditional basic sequence and nevertheless have few approximable operators in the sense that app(X) is strictly smaller than c0*(N).

evidence.quote: A Banach space X is said to have few approximable operators whenever app(X) is strictly smaller than c*_0(N).
Problem 22. Find Banach spaces with an unconditional basic sequence that have few approximable operators.

accepted.question_text: Let X_K be the C0-trivial Argyros–Haydon predual of ℓ1 mentioned in Section 2.9, and let τ_Z be the continuous singular trace on N(2/3,Z) constructed in Theorem 2.26. Describe the restriction of τ_Z to the operator ideal N(2/3,X_K)(ℓ2).

evidence.quote: Argyros–Haydon ... constructed a C0-trivial predual X_K of ℓ_1 with a basis.
Theorem 2.26. Let Z be an C-trivial Banach space. Then the value τ_Z(S) := Σ ϕ(U_i V_i) ... yields a continuous singular trace on the quasi-Banach operator ideal N(2/3,Z).
Problem 23. Describe the restriction of τ_Z to N(2/3,X_K)(ℓ2).

accepted.question_text: Let LLEX_z = H ◦ LWEYL_z be the old-fashioned left-hand extension ideal built from operators factoring through Hilbert spaces. Determine whether (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞}, or even the smaller ideal LAPP_{1,∞}, fails to be contained in LLEX_{1,∞}.

evidence.quote: Referring to [32, Sections 6.6, 7.1, and 15.6], we define the quasi-Banach operator ideal LLEX_z := H ◦ LWEYL_z, where the symbol LEX stands for left-hand extention.
Problem 24. Show that (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞}, or even LAPP_{1,∞}, is not included in LLEX_{1,∞}.

accepted.question_text: Find operator ideals, different from the examples furnished by Theorems 2.26 and 2.27, that support non-vanishing traces.

evidence.quote: Apart from Theorems 2.26 and 2.27, the only method to construct traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces is that given in the proof of Theorem 1.19.
Problem 25. Find operator ideals different from the above that support non-vanishing traces.

accepted.question_text: For every quasi-Banach operator ideal A and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals x(N0) and y(N0), determine whether there always exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) such that the reiteration identity (AAPP_x)APP_y = AAPP_z holds.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Show that, for every quasi-Banach operator ideal A and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals x(N0) and y(N0), there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) such that (AAPP_x)APP_y = AAPP_z.

accepted.question_text: Find a shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) for which the two equivalent quasi-norms on LAPP_z discussed in Theorem 1.4, namely ‖·|LAPP_z‖ and |||·|LAPP_z|||, are genuinely different on at least one operator S ∈ LAPP_z(X,Y).

evidence.quote: Let z(N0) be any quasi-normed shift-monotone sequence ideal. As shown in Theorem 1.4, the quasi-norms ‖·|LAPP_z‖ and ||| · |LAPP_z||| are equivalent.
Problem 27. Find z(N0) such that the quasi-norms ‖S|LAPP_z‖ and |||S|LAPP_z||| are different for some S ∈ LAPP_z(X, Y ).

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the Springer full-text PDF and mapped Section 2 'Open Problems' to pages 23–42, with numbered Problems 1–27 on pages 26–42.
Extracted all 27 explicit numbered problems from subsections 2.1 through 2.12 and treated them as the complete candidate set.
Rewrote each numbered problem into a standalone question by inlining the local meaning of the relevant operator ideals, spectra, or trace constructions when the same paper defined them explicitly.

Accepted all 27 numbered problems. Each accepted row has verbatim page-cited evidence and is marked unsolved because the source presents them as open problems and does not explicitly mark any as solved within the same source artifact.
